document.title: [Title Excised] Usama Bin Ladin's Islamic Army Issued a Series of Fatwas, Most of the Against the United States
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Central Intelligence Agency 9/11 File: Hundreds of Secret Agency Documents on Osama Bin Laden Declassified
document.note: CIA Intelligence Report on a series of fatwas issued by the Islamic Army, most against the United States. Source: 9/11 Commission Report, Chapter 4, Endnote 3.

persons.name: Usama Bin Ladin
persons.role: Leader of the 'Islamic Army' that issued a series of fatwas, mostly against the United States

organizations.name: Islamic Army
organizations.notes: Described as issuing fatwas, most against the United States, authorizing attacks on U.S. forces worldwide and in Saudi Arabia.

organizations.name: United States
organizations.notes: Target of the fatwas; U.S. forces named as legitimate targets.

places.name: Saudi Arabia
places.significance: One fatwa declared the Islamic Army could attack U.S. forces in Saudi Arabia.

events.description: CIA cable reports that Bin Ladin's Islamic Army issued a series of fatwas, mostly against the US: legal to fight US forces anywhere; permitted to attack US forces in Saudi Arabia, citing Koran 'fight all of them as they fight all of you'; another on attacking forces in another location; and a ruling regarding killing of noncombatant US citizens.

A CIA cable reports that Usama Bin Ladin's Islamic Army issued a series of fatwas, most of them against the United States. One fatwa held it legal to fight U.S. forces anywhere in the world. Another allowed attacks on U.S. forces in Saudi Arabia, citing the Koranic passage 'fight all of them as they fight all of you.'

relationships.detail: The cable refers to Bin Ladin's Islamic Army issuing fatwas.
Fatwas authorize fighting US forces anywhere in the world and in Saudi Arabia.
relationships.quote: IT WAS LEGAL UNDER ISLAMIC LAW FOR THE ISLAMIC ARMY TO FIGHT U.S. FORCES ANYWHERE IN THE WORLD

relationships.detail: A fatwa declared that the Islamic Army could attack U.S. forces in Saudi Arabia, so the country is named as a target location.
relationships.quote: ANOTHER DECLARED THAT THE ISLAMIC ARMY COULD ATTACK U.S. FORCES IN SAUDI ARABIA.

relationships.detail: U.S. forces are described as present in Saudi Arabia, where the fatwa permits attacks on them.
relationships.quote: ATTACK U.S. FORCES IN SAUDI ARABIA.

key_claims: In January 1997 CIA reported that Bin Ladin's Islamic Army had issued several fatwas, mostly against the United States.
One fatwa held it legal to fight U.S. forces anywhere in the world.
Another authorized attacks on U.S. forces in Saudi Arabia, based on Koranic verses.
A further fatwa addressed the killing of noncombatant U.S. citizens in the course of attacks on U.S. forces.
